text: ServiceNow Flow Designer & Automation, back in course 4, had you drop a generic REST step into a Flow and call a spoke action someone else had already built. That lesson was about using IntegrationHub from inside the flow canvas. This chapter goes a level deeper: understanding what IntegrationHub actually is as a product, what it costs an organization to turn on, and — by Lesson 18 — how to build a brand-new spoke action yourself, something course 4 never asked you to do.

Here's the detail earlier lessons glossed over: IntegrationHub is not bundled into every ServiceNow edition the way basic Flow Designer is. Depending on the customer's contract, it ships as a separately-licensed add-on — the same commercial pattern you saw with Performance Analytics back in course 2's Reporting & Dashboards material. Before you design a solution around a spoke, or a custom action, you confirm the instance actually has an IntegrationHub entitlement. Designing around capabilities the customer hasn't licensed is a mistake that tends to surface late, usually in a demo, never during a design review.

IntegrationHub's first value proposition is Spokes — packaged, ServiceNow-maintained sets of actions for a specific external system: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Workday, and dozens more. Before IntegrationHub, connecting a Flow to Slack meant hand-rolling a REST Message, hand-coding the authentication handshake, and maintaining all of that whenever Slack changed its API. A Spoke replaces that with a drop-in action ServiceNow itself keeps current. The second value proposition is the generic REST and SOAP steps living directly on the flow canvas for systems with no official spoke at all.

A real-world flow often leans on both propositions in the very same run: a Slack spoke action posts a notification, while a generic REST step in that same flow calls a niche internal system that no spoke covers. Spokes handle the common, well-known integrations that ServiceNow itself maintains. The generic REST and SOAP steps handle everything else, configured directly where you need them, using an Authentication Profile the same way any REST call in this course has.

Together, those two capabilities mean a flow builder rarely needs to drop into a Script step just to make an outbound call — which is exactly the gap IntegrationHub exists to close. Next up: what a Spoke actually looks like once you open it up, and how its individual Connector Actions are structured underneath.
